videos.title: Usability 101
videos.creator: NNgroup — Kate Kaplan
videos.course_fit: Aula 2 pages 28–37 and HTML lesson hci-usability. Nielsen's five quality components complement, rather than replace, the lecture's effectiveness–efficiency–satisfaction definition.
videos.watch_plan: Watch once, then revisit the usability lesson. Pause to explain each quality component with your own unrelated example.
videos.practice: Explain why a fast interface can still fail the user's goal; distinguish effectiveness from efficiency.
videos.duration: About 4 minutes (rounded duration on official NN/G video page)

videos.title: Five User Interview Mistakes to Avoid (in 5 Minutes)
videos.creator: NNgroup — Therese Fessenden
videos.course_fit: Phase 1 real-user interviews. Demonstrates interviewer behaviour that can distort the evidence.
videos.watch_plan: Watch before practising an interview. List the mistakes without looking, then rehearse neutral follow-up questions.
videos.practice: Rewrite one leading question as a neutral question and give one probing follow-up. Do not invent participants or findings.
videos.duration: About 6 minutes (official NN/G page; the title says 5 minutes)

videos.title: What Are Personas and Why Should I Care?
videos.creator: NNgroup — Kim Flaherty
videos.course_fit: Phase 1 representative personas. Introductory purpose and use of personas; not a full analysis tutorial.
videos.watch_plan: Watch after reviewing the persona requirement. Explain how a persona should change one design decision.
videos.practice: Distinguish an evidence-backed user pattern from an invented biography. State what research evidence would justify a persona attribute.
videos.duration: About 2 minutes (rounded duration on official NN/G video page)

videos.title: How to Empathy Map
videos.creator: NNgroup — Sarah Gibbons
videos.course_fit: Phase 1 empathy maps. Provides a five-step creation process and helps distinguish evidence from assumptions.
videos.watch_plan: Watch, then sketch the map categories from memory using an unrelated practice scenario.
videos.practice: Explain which entries require real observations or statements, and label untested assumptions as hypotheses.
videos.duration: About 3 minutes (rounded duration on official NN/G video page)

videos.title: Customer Journey Mapping 101
videos.creator: NNgroup — Sarah Gibbons
videos.course_fit: Phase 1 journey maps. Customer/service examples need adaptation to the actual course context; video does not supply research findings.
videos.watch_plan: Watch after the empathy-map introduction. Draw the five components and explain their relationship.
videos.practice: Explain the difference between a journey map and an interface click sequence. Identify which parts of a journey require research evidence.
videos.duration: About 2 minutes (rounded duration on official NN/G video page)

videos.title: Paper Prototyping 101
videos.creator: NNgroup — Rachel Krause
videos.course_fit: Phase 2 paper tests and the Aula 2 iterative-design lesson. Helps test interaction ideas before medium/high-fidelity implementation; does not teach a particular prototyping application's controls.
videos.watch_plan: Watch this short introduction before a paper-prototype practice block. Pause to describe how the user can interact with a paper interface and how a design change could be made immediately.
videos.practice: For an unrelated practice interface, sketch two small screens and one realistic task; explain what observation would make you revise the sketch. Do not report a practice rehearsal as real project testing.
videos.duration: About 3 minutes (rounded duration on official NN/G video page)

videos.title: How to Conduct a Heuristic Evaluation
videos.creator: NNgroup — Kate Moran
videos.course_fit: Phase 2 cross-group Nielsen heuristic report. Explains a systematic review process; evaluator findings are potential issues, not observations of real users. Apply the course's report/rating instructions where they differ.
videos.watch_plan: Watch the official NN/G video page, then practise one inspection on an unrelated interface. Name the heuristic and record the specific issue before discussing a proposed improvement.
videos.practice: Explain the difference between expert inspection and user testing. Describe how you would document one potential violation and its user consequence without inventing test data.
videos.duration: About 5 minutes (individual official NN/G video page; topic index rounds it to 4)

videos.title: Usability Testing 101
videos.creator: NNgroup — Kate Moran
videos.course_fit: Phase 3 real-user usability testing and Aula 2 representative-user evaluation. Introductory method; it does not teach SUS scoring, quantitative sample-size calculation or replace the course's required participant count and metrics.
videos.watch_plan: Watch before preparing a real-user test protocol. Explain facilitator, task and participant from memory, then check the course requirements for measurements and consent.
videos.practice: Write one neutral task prompt for an unrelated practice interface and list what you would observe. Explain why completing the task for the participant would bias the result.
videos.duration: About 2 minutes (rounded duration on official NN/G video page)

videos.title: Reflection: Gulfs of Evaluation and Execution — Intro to the Design of Everyday Things
videos.creator: Udacity — official Intro to the Design of Everyday Things course
videos.course_fit: Aula 2 pages 10–14 and HTML lesson hci-norman. Official course reflection on the two gulfs; not a complete explanation of all seven stages or of Abowd–Beale. Supplement with the lecture and retained NN/G article.
videos.watch_plan: Watch the reflection clip within a 10-minute cap, then read the NN/G two-gulfs article or the Norman lesson. Map one unrelated interaction into the full seven stages using the course notes.
videos.practice: For a timer, distinguish not knowing how to start it from not knowing whether it started. Identify the relevant gulf and justify it. Use Moodle notes to check the complete seven-stage cycle.
